abstract.p: The Alia musica is transmitted in 14 manuscripts from different centuries and locations, either presenting the full text or excerpts and compilations. Respecting the manuscripts as documents of individual scribal intentions or specific institutional demands, each extant copy from the Alia musica is edited separately. The apparatus represents the differences between the manuscript and the edited texts and reports particuliarities regarding the text’s materiality and semantics. The individual readings of the different manuscripts can be compared using the synopsis. Quotations or paraphrases from earlier texts can be compared with their source-texts. The translations provided refer to the individual text of each manuscript.

The critical apparatus refers exclusively to the edited manuscript. It reports all the differences between the edited text and the manuscript, as well as peculiarities regarding the text’s materiality and semantics. The differences are highlighted as one moves the cursor over the edited text.
All instances of interlinear and marginal glosses are displayed here.
All quotations or paraphrases of ancient or medieval source-texts are displayed here, providing the source-texts themselves, based on their reference-edition, in a separate column.
Here one finds a synoptical display of the readings of each sentence throughout the manuscript-transmission as one moves the cursor over the edited text.
Here one finds an English translation of the individual manuscript’s specific text.

p.seg: De harmonica consideratione Boetius ita disseruit:
Quia neque solum in terminis speculationem proportionis habet, neque solum in differentiis, sed in utrisque communiter,

querit enim ut quemadmodum sunt ad se extremi termini, sic maioris ad medium differentia contra differentiam
medietatis ad ultimum.
Ipsarum quoque abbreviation clarified by different hand musicarum consonantiarum, quas symphonias nominant, proportiones in hac poene paene sola medietate frequenter inuenies.
Namque symphonia diatesseron quae princeps est et quodammodo uim obtinet elementi, in eiusmodi harmonicis medietatibus inuenitur, ut sunt VI ad VIII.
Sint ergo huiusmodi medietatis termini, quorum extremi sint dupli, et alii quorum extremi sint tripli, ita:

figure.note: The text implies two separate number series as individual diagrams, which were erroneously joined together into a single number series in this manuscript during the process of framing.

p.seg: Duodenarius igitur ad senarium duplus est;
et in alia dispositione XII ad IIII triplus est.
Horum si differentias colligamus et ad se inuicem comparemus, epitrita proportio, id est idem diatessaron sinphonia colligitur.
Inter VI enim et duodecim senarius est, et inter IIII et duodecim octonarius ad senarium ad senariu sesquitertiam efficit proportionem.
In eadem quoque medietate et diapente sinphonia componitur.
In duplici, uidelicet XII ad VIII, et in triplici, VI ad IIII, sesqualtera est.
Post hunc autem diapason consonantia est, ut VI ad XII.
In triplici quoque dispositione simul diapente et diapason simphonia corrected into "simphonja" by different hand componitur, ut sunt
Et quoniam triplus duas continet consonantias, diapente scilicet ac diapason, in differentiis eiusdem triplicis eundem triplum reperiemus.
Nam inter VI et VIIII corrected from "VIII" by different hand ternarius differentia est, et inter VIIII et XVIII nouenarius, qui ad ternarium triplus est.
In dupla uero dispositione, maior terminus differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est.
